Cos
KOSS
proper noun
An island of the Aegean Sea, off the coast of Asia Minor, at which Paul’s ship touched on his voyage toward Jerusalem; spelled Coos in the Authorized Version.

📖 Biblical Definition

Cos, spelled Coos in the Authorized Version, was an island of the Aegean Sea off the coast of Asia Minor, one of the stages of Paul’s last voyage toward Jerusalem. After the sorrowful parting from the elders of Ephesus at Miletus, Luke records the daily run of the ship: “it came to pass, that after we were gotten from them, and had launched, we came with a straight course unto Coos, and the day following unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara” (Act 21:1). Cos was a night’s anchorage on a straight and prosperous run, one link in the chain of ports that carried the apostle nearer to the city where bonds awaited him. The very ordinariness of the notice is instructive: the servant of God is borne along, day by day, port by port, by winds and providences he does not govern, yet all working to set him where God would have him. Even the straight course and fair wind to Cos were of the Lord, who orders the seas and the ways of His servants. The island stands, like Trogyllium and Rhodes and Patara, as a small witness that no stage of a believer’s journey is outside the ordering of God: the smooth days as well as the storms, the fair winds as well as the foul, are all appointed to bring the servant to his place and his work. The Lord directeth the steps, and the sea-miles, of them that are His.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

An Aegean island where Paul’s ship touched on his way to Jerusalem; a witness that God orders every stage of His servants’ journey, the fair days as well as the storms.

expand to see more

COS, an island of the Aegean Sea, off the coast of Asia Minor.

Spelled Coos, Paul’s ship touched there on his voyage to Jerusalem (Act 21:1).

It lay on a straight and prosperous run after leaving Miletus.

It was one link in the chain of ports bearing Paul on.

It witnesses that God orders every stage of His servants’ journey.

📖 Key Scripture

Act 21:1 — "And it came to pass, that after we were gotten from them, and had launched, we came with a straight course unto Coos, and the day following unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara:"

Act 21:5 — "And when we had accomplished those days, we departed and went our way; and they all brought us on our way, with wives and children, till we were out of the city: and we kneeled down on the shore, and prayed."

Psa 37:23 — "The steps of a good man are ordered by the LORD: and he delighteth in his way."

Pro 20:24 — "Man's goings are of the LORD; how can a man then understand his own way?"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

An island of Scripture, a stage of Paul’s voyage; it recovers the truth that God orders every step of His servants’ way, the fair days as well as the storms.

expand to see more

Cos faces no postmodern redefinition. The truth its quiet anchorage carries answers the notion that only the great crises and storms of life are governed by God, while the ordinary, prosperous days run on by chance apart from His care.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is God’s ordering of the whole journey. The straight course and fair wind to Cos were as much of the Lord as the later storm and shipwreck. No stage of a believer’s way, smooth or rough, is outside His ordering; the steps of a good man are ordered by the LORD, who directeth the very sea-miles of His servants.
